- I have felt that Jonathan is hiding something important from me. This made me anxious and suspicious, so I arranged to meet him at our favorite coffee shop to confront him.
- At the coffee shop, I told Jonathan I felt he was hiding something. He said I should trust him, but then admitted he had been keeping something from me: he is in some trouble and did not know how to tell me.
- After learning this, I felt worried and empathetic. I offered to help him, said he is my best friend, and promised to do everything I can. Jonathan said the situation is complicated, he didn’t want to drag me into it, but then said he could use support and resources to get out of his mess.
- I later suspected Jonathan’s trouble might be related to criminal activity. I asked if it was illegal. Jonathan said he couldn’t say for sure; he might have gotten involved with the wrong people, but he did not do anything illegal himself. He thanked me and said he trusts me to handle it carefully.
- I told Jonathan I would look into the matter discreetly to make sure he is safe.
- My investigation gave me news/leads that Jonathan is being framed—that someone is trying to set him up. I told Jonathan I believe he is being framed, that I’m not sure yet who is responsible, but I have leads. I said I would gather more evidence to prove his innocence. Jonathan reacted with surprise and gratitude.
- I have now found out/come to believe that the person behind this is someone both Jonathan and I know and trust. I feel betrayed and resolute. I told Jonathan this and said I will confront the real culprit and make sure they are brought to justice. Jonathan warned me the person is dangerous but said he trusts me to do what is right.
- Relevant prior relationship: Jonathan and I have been close friends since childhood. I often seek his advice on personal and professional matters, and I value his perspective.

I do not have access to hidden events, private information Jonathan has not told me, or facts known only to the narrator/reader.
